title: Verbes en -IR et -RE (présent)
ruleNote: After the -ER verbs, French has two more regular families: verbs ending in -IR (finir, choisir) and -RE (vendre, attendre). You remove the ending to get the stem, then add a fixed set of endings. The -IR group adds a special -iss- in the plural; the -RE group keeps things short, even dropping the ending entirely for il/elle.

elements.label: L'infinitif en -IR
elements.ruleNote: A second verb family ends in -IR: finir, choisir. Remove -IR to find the stem (fin-, chois-) before adding endings.

examples.prompt: Quel est le radical de « finir » ?
examples.explanation: Remove -ir from finir to get the stem fin-.
examples.translation: The stem of finir is fin-.

examples.prompt: Quel est le radical de « choisir » ?
examples.explanation: Remove -ir from choisir to get the stem chois-.
examples.translation: The stem of choisir is chois-.

examples.explanation: After veux, the second verb stays in the infinitive finir.
examples.hint: Two verbs: the second stays as -ir.

examples.explanation: After aime, the second verb stays in the infinitive choisir.

examples.prompt: Quel mot est un infinitif en -IR ?
examples.explanation: Only finir is the infinitive; the others are conjugated.
After dois, the verb stays in the infinitive choisir.

elements.label: je / tu / il + -is, -is, -it
elements.ruleNote: Singular -IR endings: je finis, tu finis, il finit. The first two sound the same; -t marks the il/elle form in writing.

examples.explanation: For je, finir becomes finis.
For tu, choisir becomes choisis.
For il, finir takes -t: il finit.
For elle, choisir becomes choisit with -t.
For tu, choisir becomes choisis.
je choisis; l' attaches to eau before a vowel.

elements.label: nous + -issons
elements.ruleNote: For nous, regular -IR verbs add -issons: nous finissons, nous choisissons. The extra -iss- is the signature of this group.

examples.explanation: For nous, finir becomes finissons with -iss-.
For nous, choisir becomes choisissons with -iss-.
For nous, the form is finissons.
nous choisissons keeps the -iss-.
For nous, the form is choisissons.
nous finissons with the -iss- signature.

elements.label: vous + -issez
elements.ruleNote: For vous, add -issez: vous finissez, vous choisissez. Note the same -iss- as in the nous form.

examples.explanation: For vous, finir becomes finissez with -iss-.
For vous, choisir becomes choisissez with -iss-.
For vous, the form is finissez.
vous choisissez keeps the -iss-.
For vous, the form is choisissez.
vous finissez with the -iss- signature.

elements.label: ils / elles + -issent
elements.ruleNote: For ils/elles, add -issent: ils finissent, elles choisissent. The -ent is silent, but the -iss- is heard.

examples.explanation: For ils, finir becomes finissent with -iss-.
For elles, choisir becomes choisissent with -iss-.
For ils, the form is finissent.
elles choisissent; l' attaches to école before a vowel.
For elles, the form is finissent.
ils choisissent keeps the -iss-.

elements.label: Conjugaison complète : finir
elements.ruleNote: The full -IR model: je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent. Learn it as one block.

examples.explanation: je finis: singular -is.
tu finis: same as the je form.
nous finissons: plural -issons.
il finit: singular -it.
ils finissent: plural -issent.
vous finissez: plural -issez.

elements.label: Le verbe choisir
elements.ruleNote: 'choisir' (to choose) follows finir exactly: je choisis, nous choisissons, ils choisissent.

examples.explanation: je choisis: singular -is.
tu choisis: same as the je form.
nous choisissons: plural -issons.
elle choisit: singular -it.
ils choisissent: plural -issent.
vous choisissez; l' attaches to eau before a vowel.

elements.label: Le -iss- au pluriel
elements.ruleNote: The key feature of these verbs is the -iss- in all three plural forms: -issons, -issez, -issent. The singular has no -iss-.

examples.explanation: The nous form has -iss-: finissons.
The vous form has -iss-: choisissez.
ils finissent keeps the -iss- of the plural.

examples.prompt: Quelle forme n'a PAS le -iss- ? (finir, je)
examples.explanation: The je form finis has NO -iss-; it is singular.
examples.translation: The singular je finis has no -iss-.

examples.explanation: nous choisissons keeps the plural -iss-.
The elles form has -iss-: choisissent.

elements.label: -IR vs -ER (nous)
elements.ruleNote: Don't mix families: -ER gives 'nous parlons', -IR gives 'nous finissons'. The endings differ, so check the infinitive first.

examples.explanation: parler is -ER, so nous parlons, no -iss-.
finir is -IR, so nous finissons with -iss-.
manger is -ER, so nous mangeons, no -iss-.
choisir is -IR, so nous choisissons with -iss-.
aimer is -ER, so nous aimons, no -iss-.
finir is -IR, so nous finissons with -iss-.

elements.label: L'infinitif en -RE
elements.ruleNote: A third family ends in -RE: vendre, attendre. Remove -RE to find the stem (vend-, attend-).

examples.prompt: Quel est le radical de « vendre » ?
examples.explanation: Remove -re from vendre to get the stem vend-.
examples.translation: The stem of vendre is vend-.

examples.prompt: Quel est le radical de « attendre » ?
examples.explanation: Remove -re from attendre to get the stem attend-.
examples.translation: The stem of attendre is attend-.

examples.explanation: After veux, the second verb stays in the infinitive vendre.
After aime, the second verb stays in the infinitive attendre.

examples.prompt: Quel mot est un infinitif en -RE ?
examples.explanation: Only vendre is the infinitive; the others are conjugated.
After dois, the verb stays in the infinitive attendre.

elements.label: je / tu + -s, -s
elements.ruleNote: Singular -RE endings start with -s: je vends, tu vends, j'attends, tu attends. Both forms sound the same.

examples.explanation: For je, vendre becomes vends with -s.
For tu, vendre becomes vends, same as je.

examples.prompt: Construis : « I wait for the bus. »
examples.explanation: je becomes j' before a vowel: j'attends.
For tu, attendre becomes attends with -s.
For je, vendre becomes vends with -s.

examples.prompt: Construis : « You wait for the friend. »
examples.explanation: tu attends; l' attaches to ami before a vowel.

elements.label: il / elle : pas de terminaison
elements.ruleNote: For il/elle, regular -RE verbs add nothing to the stem: il vend, elle attend. The bare stem is the whole form.

examples.explanation: For il, vendre is just vend, no ending.

examples.prompt: Construis : « She waits for the bus. »
examples.explanation: For elle, attendre is just attend, no ending.
il vend has no ending after the stem.
elle attend has no ending after the stem.
elle vend: the bare stem is the whole form.

examples.prompt: Construis : « He waits for the friend. »
examples.explanation: il attend; l' attaches to amie before a vowel.

elements.label: nous + -ons
elements.ruleNote: For nous, -RE verbs add -ons: nous vendons, nous attendons. Simpler than the -IR -issons form.

examples.explanation: For nous, vendre becomes vendons, no -iss-.

examples.prompt: Construis : « We wait for the bus. »
examples.explanation: For nous, attendre becomes attendons, no -iss-.
For nous, the form is vendons.
For nous, the form is attendons.
nous vendons: simple -ons ending.

examples.prompt: Construis : « We wait for the friend. »
examples.explanation: nous attendons; l' attaches to amie before a vowel.

elements.label: vous + -ez
elements.ruleNote: For vous, add -ez: vous vendez, vous attendez. Same -ez ending you met with -ER verbs.

examples.explanation: For vous, vendre becomes vendez, no -iss-.

examples.prompt: Construis : « You wait for the train. »
examples.explanation: For vous, attendre becomes attendez, no -iss-.
For vous, the form is vendez.
For vous, the form is attendez.
vous vendez: simple -ez ending.

examples.prompt: Construis : « You wait for the school. »
examples.explanation: vous attendez; l' attaches to école before a vowel.

elements.label: ils / elles + -ent
elements.ruleNote: For ils/elles, add -ent: ils vendent, elles attendent. The -ent is silent, so you hear the stem's final consonant.

examples.explanation: For ils, vendre becomes vendent, no -iss-.

examples.prompt: Construis : « They wait for the bus. »
examples.explanation: For elles, attendre becomes attendent, no -iss-.
For ils, the form is vendent.
For elles, the form is attendent.
ils vendent: silent -ent ending.

examples.prompt: Construis : « They wait for the friend. »
examples.explanation: elles attendent; l' attaches to amie before a vowel.

elements.label: Conjugaison complète : vendre
elements.ruleNote: The full -RE model: je vends, tu vends, il vend, nous vendons, vous vendez, ils vendent. Note il vend has no ending.

examples.explanation: je vends: singular -s.
tu vends: same as the je form.
il vend: no ending after the stem.
nous vendons: -ons ending.
ils vendent: silent -ent ending.
vous vendez: -ez ending.

elements.label: Le verbe attendre
elements.ruleNote: 'attendre' (to wait) follows vendre: j'attends, il attend, nous attendons, ils attendent.

examples.prompt: Construis : « I wait for the train. »
examples.explanation: j'attends: je becomes j' before a vowel.
tu attends: same as the j' form.
elle attend: no ending after the stem.

examples.prompt: Construis : « We wait for the bus. »
examples.explanation: nous attendons: -ons ending.

examples.prompt: Construis : « They wait for the train. »
examples.explanation: ils attendent: silent -ent ending.
vous attendez: -ez ending.

elements.label: Choisir la bonne famille
elements.ruleNote: Check the infinitive ending first: -ER, -IR, or -RE decides the endings. 'finir' → -is, 'vendre' → -s, 'parler' → -e.

examples.explanation: finir is -IR, so je finis with -is.
vendre is -RE, so je vends with -s.
parler is -ER, so je parle with -e.
choisir is -IR, so elle choisit with -it.
vendre is -RE, so il vend with no ending.
aimer is -ER, so il aime with -e.

elements.label: Forme négative et objet
elements.ruleNote: These verbs negate and take objects like the others: 'je ne vends pas la voiture', 'elle attend le bus'. The frame hugs the verb.

examples.prompt: Construis : « I do not sell the car. »
examples.explanation: ne ... pas wraps the verb vends.
examples.translation: I do not sell the car.

examples.prompt: Construis : « She waits for the bus. »
examples.explanation: elle attend takes a direct object: le bus.

examples.prompt: Construis : « We do not finish the work. »
examples.explanation: ne ... pas wraps the verb finissons.
examples.translation: We do not finish the work.

examples.prompt: Construis : « He does not wait for the train. »
examples.explanation: ne becomes n' before the vowel of attend.
examples.translation: He does not wait for the train.

examples.prompt: Complète : « Je ne ___ pas le livre. » (finir)
examples.explanation: je finis stays the same inside ne ... pas.
examples.translation: I do not finish the book.

examples.prompt: Construis : « They do not sell the house. »
examples.explanation: ne ... pas wraps the verb vendent.
examples.translation: They do not sell the house.

elements.label: Synthèse : verbes en -IR et -RE
elements.ruleNote: Put it together: spot the family, take the stem, add the right ending (remembering -iss- for -IR plurals), and finish the sentence.

examples.explanation: -IR plural nous finissons keeps the -iss-.
-RE il vend: bare stem, no ending.
-IR tu choisis with -is.

examples.prompt: Construis : « You wait for the bus. »
examples.explanation: -RE vous attendez with -ez.
-IR ils finissent keeps the -iss-.

examples.prompt: Construis : « They wait for the friend. »
examples.explanation: -RE elles attendent with silent -ent.
